newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich says "making progress" on budget talks.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich says "making progress" on budget talks.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Wednesday progress was being made in budget negotiations and that pressure from the appropriations process meant some movement was needed "fairly soon."
"We're making progress ... we need to move something fairly soon, but I have hopes we'll get something done," the Georgia Republican told reporters.
Pressure from the appropriations process "is very important," Gingrich said, noting that without a budget, Congress cannot move on appropriations.
Gingrich said House Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich, an Ohio Republican, "reports that there's very serious conversations underway."

"It would be better the earlier we can get to an agreement so that we can begin to move the appropriations process, the better off we are. And frankly I'd like to have started moving a couple of weeks ago," Gingrich said. "It seemed to us the chance of getting an agreement was worth the extra time," he added.
